title: Metric accuracy of a toed-in side-by-side stereo webcam

method.target: rigid textured box, face perpendicular to the optical axis, filling the central patch
method.distance_measurement: tape measure, camera front face to box front face
method.disparity_statistic: median over the central 120x120 px patch, then median over 12 consecutive frames
method.note: min_disparity must be negative: the sensors are toed in, so disparity is negative beyond the convergence distance. Samples at 0.310-0.720 m were taken before that was known, with min_disparity=0; their disparities are positive and unaffected by the search floor.

held_out_note: Measured after the calibration was fitted and never used in it. A fourth reading nominally at 1.00 m gave -5.19 px, all but identical to the 1.10 m sample; the box had already been moved, so it is excluded as a mislabelled distance rather than a measurement error.

search_floor_comparison.description: Same scene, box at 1.26 m, with and without a negative disparity search.

matcher_comparison.description: One frame, 640x480 per eye, min_disparity=-48. Edge agreement is the mean horizontal image-gradient magnitude at pixels where the disparity gradient exceeds 2 px, i.e. whether depth discontinuities coincide with image edges.

contrast_equalisation_bias_check.description: Same 12 frames, one scene, with and without CLAHE. Identical disparity means the sharper edges cost nothing in measured distance.

limitations: Depth scale only. Lens distortion and residual sensor misalignment are uncorrected, so accuracy degrades away from the image centre; every measurement here is from the central patch and is therefore a best case.
Distances were set by hand against a tape, reproducible to a few millimetres at best. One nominal distance proved stale by ~90 mm and was excluded.
Single scene, single session, one camera unit. No claim is made about unit-to-unit variation or about temperature or focus drift.

The residual is systematically negative at all three held-out distances, consistent with the tape origin sitting ahead of the optical centre by roughly a centimetre, which a chessboard calibration would resolve.
Rolling shutter was not characterised and matters more than depth error for a moving robot.
